statement.p: The figure below shows the level curves of a function f(x,y) around a maximum or minimum, M. The x- and y-axes are along the bottom and left edge of the figure, respectively.

One of the points P and Q has coordinates (x_1,y_1) and the other has coordinates (x_2, y_2). Suppose b \lt 0 and c > 0. Consider the two linear approximations to f given by f(x,y) \approx a+b(x-x_1)+c(y-y_1), and f(x,y) \approx k+m(x-x_2)+n(y-y_2).
(a) What is the relationship between the values of a and k?
(b) What are the coordinates of P?

(c) Is M a maximum or a minimum?
?
maximum
minimum
(d) What can you say about the sign of the constants m and n?

static.solution:
(a) Since P and Q lie on the same level curve, we have a=k.
(b) We have b=f_x and c=f_y. Since the gradient of f at P (respectively Q) points toward M or away from M, from the figure, we see f_x(P) and f_y(P) have opposite signs, while f_x(Q) and f_y(Q) have the same signs. Thus Q is the point (x_2,y_2), and P is (x_1,y_1).
(c) Since b=f_x(P) \lt 0 and c=f_y(P) > 0, the value of f must increase as we go away from M. Thus, M must be a minimum.
(d) Since M is a minimum, m > 0 and n > 0.
